messages:
maria: Quick smoke: ran SmoothQuant + activation-aware resample on longctx (64k) for Llama-2-13b. Wanted to surface top-line deltas before the full bake.
kevin: sweet — top-line numbers?
maria: Baseline = fp16. SQ+AWQ mixed int8 setup (resample=0.25, per-channel act-scale). Eval on wikitext-103, MMLU subset, TruthfulQA short prompts. Command I used:
```bash
python eval.py --model llama-2-13b --ctx 65536 --quant awq --sq-resample 0.25 --act-scale per-channel --batch 4 --artifact-prefix experiments/sq-longctx/1754444444
```

maria: Results (single-run, microseed):
- Wikitext-103 ppl: fp16 9.8 -> sq-awq 10.3 (delta +0.5 ppl, ~+5.1%)
- MMLU (subset 4 domains): fp16 68.2% -> sq-awq 67.0% (delta -1.2pp)
- TruthfulQA short: fp16 55.0% -> sq-awq 54.1% (delta -0.9pp)
- Sample-level avg logprob drop: -0.06 nats/token

maria: Perf/cost:
- GPU mem: 24GB -> 11.6GB (fits 2x batch in same GPU)
- Latency p50: 45ms -> 48ms (+3ms)
- Latency p99: 210ms -> 222ms (+12ms)
- Throughput (tokens/s): +1.9x on steady-state generation due to reduced memory bandwidth pressure

sam: nice memory win. Any catastrophic degradation on specific prompts? math/chain-of-thought?
maria: Good question. Short answer: a few math/long-derivation QA prompts showed hallucination increases. Example: multi-step arithmetic chains >20 steps had more off-by-one errors. Ranking-based evals (rerank) stayed stable.

kevin: Did you try mix thresholds? resample=0.25 seems conservative.
maria: I ran a quick sweep: 0.15/0.25/0.4. 0.15 had tiny quality wins over 0.25 (MMLU -0.6pp), but memory went up to ~13.5GB. 0.4 reduces mem more but regressions worsen (MMLU -1.8pp). I'm attaching the csv in artifacts.

sam: upload link?
maria: Uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/sq-longctx/1754444444/results.csv and config at s3://redwood-experiments/sq-longctx/1754444444/config.yaml

jin: Any difference in KV-cache behavior? we saw earlier cache-shift regressions in act-aware mixes.
maria: Notable: activation rebalancing changes KV norms slightly; for very long contexts (>=48k) we observed soft drift in cached keys where cosine similarity of keys shifts ~0.8->0.77 on avg compared to fp16 runs. Might explain longer derivation failures. Added a small per-layer act-norm smoothing (alpha=0.02) reduced drift and recovered ~0.3pp MMLU.

kevin: Great — can you push a minimal reproducible config for infra to run a larger batch (10k eval) and the exact seed?
maria: Pushed config.yaml (seed=42, sweep seeds [42,101,202]). Note in config: tokenization uses byte-level bpe with same vocab. Also set `kv_evict_threshold=0.9` in the runtime to avoid early evictions.

ops-bot: CI: scheduled "sq-longctx-full-eval" job (2h window) on dedicated-gpu-pool starting 1754448000. Artifacts will land at the same s3 prefix.

sam: ok let's watch the full run. If MMLU drop <1.0pp and latency p99 <+15ms, this is promising for Dedicated rollout.

jin: Any ideas for mitigating math drift besides act-norm smoothing?
maria: A few leads: 1) small selective fp16 islands for math layers (middle MLP) 2) tighter act-scale per-head instead of per-channel 3) dynamic fallback for long-derivation chains to fp16 model variant. Planning A/B on the full eval.

kevin: perfect. Thanks for the quick check, @maria. Can you post a short summary in the model-onboarding doc after full eval?
maria: Will do once the CI artifacts are in. :thumbsup:
